name: hazard-screening-rules
licence: UNRESOLVED — no licence statement accompanies this table, in this repository or in the one it was ported from. Do not read this field as a grant. See retrieved_from for what is known and what a reviewer still has to decide.
retrieved_from: Ported byte-for-byte from Chemclaw3's `src/chemclaw/science/safety/rules.yaml` (D-080, D-086), where it was written as first-party content: eleven structural SMARTS and five pairwise-incompatibility SMARTS, each composed in that repository against a named source rather than copied out of one. The sources every rule cites are Bretherick's Handbook of Reactive Chemical Hazards, 8th ed. (azides, diazonium salts, peroxides, nitrate esters, polynitroaryl compounds, perchlorates, hydrazines, N-haloamines, oxidant/reductant mixtures, peroxide/ketone, metal hydrides); Bräse et al., Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2005, 44, 5188; Green et al., Org. Process Res. Dev. 2020, 24, 67; Buckley et al., Org. Process Res. Dev. 2021, 25, 587; and Peet & Weber, Chem. Eng. News 1988, 66(31), 2. Nothing is fetched at runtime and no address here is read by any code.
description: Sixteen deterministic hazard-screening rules — eleven structural motifs (organic, non-carbon and acyl azides, diazo, diazonium, peroxide, nitrate ester, polynitroaromatic, perchlorate, hydrazine, N-halamine) and five pairwise incompatibilities checked across a reaction's components — each with a severity, an explanation written for the person reading the flag, and the literature citation it rests on. THE LICENCE IS UNRESOLVED AND THAT IS A REAL BLOCKER FOR THIS CORPUS: the file carries a citation per rule and no licence statement of any kind, and this description does not invent one. The likely reason is that the SMARTS are original expressions written against cited hazard literature rather than a transcribed table, which would make them first-party content of the same owner as Chemclaw3 — but 'likely' is not a licence, and a reviewer has to settle it before this table is distributed outside the owner's own deployments. ADVISORY ONLY: a match is a structural alert for a human to assess, never a hazard assessment, and an empty result means no rule in this table matched — never that the chemistry is safe.
